subject: Deep-link RSVP trigger stitching & tracking snippets for co-hosted webinar
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: partnerships@atlascloud.com, ben@eventops.co
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deep-link RSVP trigger matrix (first draft)

Hi team —

Attached is a first-draft RSVP trigger matrix for the Sept 14 co-hosted webinar with AtlasCloud. The focus here is stitching invites across: our marketing touch, AtlasCloud’s co-email, and the event platform reminders so that:

- A registrant who clicks an Atlas co-host link gets a calendar deep-link (adds with tz) and a unique RSVP token so we can attribute attendance back to Atlas.
- Reminders sent by EventOps use the same token so downstream tracking (attended, no-show) feeds into HubSpot cleanly.
- If a registrant comes in from the partner link but later RSVPs via the Redwood landing page, we preserve attribution and update the earliest_source field.

Notes in the sheet: row-level triggers, send windows, and fallback behaviors for conflicts (e.g., double-register). Key asks:

1) Mateo — can you confirm the token format and any length limits for HubSpot custom property? I put a 32-char token in the matrix but we may need to trim.
2) Olga — we need the deep-link format for Google/Outlook calendar entries (UTC vs local TZ). Can you propose the canonical link pattern and where to host the redirect that injects the token?
3) Ben / Atlas team — can you confirm EventOps supports including arbitrary query params on their reminder links? If not, we need a redirect route.

Attachments: rsvp-trigger-matrix.xlsx (xlsx) — includes per-audience cadence + snippet examples
tracking-snippets.md (text) — snippet library for UTM + token injection

Goal: finalize by EOD Monday so CD sends can be scheduled Tue morning.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Field Marketing Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: partnerships@atlascloud.com
Date: 2026-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deep-link RSVP trigger matrix (first draft)

Marissa — thanks for the clear matrix. Quick thoughts inline.

> Attached is a first-draft RSVP trigger matrix for the Sept 14 co-hosted webinar with AtlasCloud.

Looks good. Two quick clarifications on our side: the canonical deep-link should use the redirect pattern we use for partner-attribution: https://rwd.link/evt?r=atlas&utm_campaign=september-webinar (we'll append &tok=...). That keeps all platform link lengths short and avoids long query strings inside calendar invites.

> 1) Mateo — can you confirm the token format and any length limits for HubSpot custom property? I put a 32-char token in the matrix but we may need to trim.

Mateo — if HubSpot property is a single-line text field we can comfortably store 36 chars; however integrations with EventOps (for webhooks) sometimes truncate after 40 bytes. I suggest a 20-char base62 token (enough entropy) plus an optional source prefix (e.g., ATLAS-xxxxx). That keeps URLs compact.

> 2) Olga — we need the deep-link format for Google/Outlook calendar entries (UTC vs local TZ). Can you propose the canonical link pattern and where to host the redirect that injects the token?

Proposed: host redirect on partner.redwood.com/evtdl. The redirect will accept: ?tok=XXXXXXXX&src=atlas&event=sept14. It will generate platform-specific calendar files (ics) with local timezone auto-detection via client browser. This avoids embedding TZ in the querystring. Ops: we'll need a short-lived signed token if we put any PII inside the calendar.

Small asks for the matrix: add a column for "calendar_redirect" (yes/no) and one for "signed_token_required". Also flagged that Atlas co-email must include our deep-link (not the EventOps managed join link) so that the first touch is attributed correctly.

I attached a short stub example for the redirect: partner_redirect_example.txt (inline below).

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Partnerships & Field Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ben@eventops.co, partnerships@atlascloud.com
Date: 2026-08-29T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deep-link RSVP trigger matrix (first draft)

Thanks — confirming HubSpot and tracking details.

- HubSpot property: we'll add a single-line text property "rsvp_token" (max length 50). That covers a 20-char base62 token plus 6-char source prefix.
- For attribution logic: earliest_source will be set at registration time and only updated if the new source is higher priority (we'll add mapping in the matrix).
- EventOps notes: Ben confirmed EventOps does not allow arbitrary params on their native reminder links, but they will allow us to host a redirect URL that they can drop into reminders. Ben: per our convo, we'll use rwd.link/evtr?tok=... (EventOps to call this redirect when building reminders).

Attached are the tracking snippets that Marketing Ops validated. Put these in the email template library:

- snippet: ?utm_source=atlas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=sept14_cohost&tok={{rsvp_token}}
- calendar deep-link redirect: https://partner.redwood.com/evtdl?tok={{rsvp_token}}&src=atlas

Also added HubSpot funnel stages we should sync with CS: Registered -> Reminder Sent -> Joined -> No-Show. I'll create a quick workflow to auto-update "attended=true" via EventOps webhook to HubSpot deal WD-8893.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Growth Operations | Redwood Inference

- [Mateo] Create HubSpot property and workflow; publish tracking snippets into Marketing Templates repo. ETA: Mon noon.
- [Ben / EventOps] Confirm we can place rwd.link redirect in reminder builder. Ben said yes; please share confirmation in this thread.

If all green, CD will queue sends Tue 9am PT. I also updated the workbook with the final send windows and added the UTM examples you proposed.

Thanks all — small coordination but this will give clean downstream attribution and better calendar UX for registrants.

—Marissa
